label: first copy step after <DEL> when the fed-back first token is digit 0, long sequences (L>=7)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase at recall_idx 1, the step right after <DEL> where the model has just output original token 0 and fed it back. Nearly every activation (99.6%) has that fed-back token equal to the digit 0, meaning the sequence starts with 0. Length gates it: it never fires for L<=5, fires weakly and only sometimes for L=6 (about 1.2% of mass, lowest quartile), and fires reliably for L>=7, with precision close to 1.0 there. Its mass share goes up with L (L=7 0.21, L=8 0.35, L=9 0.44). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, at other recall positions, or on other fed-back tokens apart from a handful of q/y/g/2 cases. What is being output (out_tok, next_out) has little effect.

issues: Minor: the label leaves out the weak L=6 tail. On the test split, 1005 steps at L=6, recall_idx 1, with fed-back token 0 are missed. They hold 1.3% of the activation mass and all sit at about 0.01-0.07 of the max activation. The explanation already describes them correctly and they are not a systematic counterexample class.

Every claim I checked holds. Firing is 100% in the copy phase and 100% at recall_idx 1. The fed-back token is 0 in 9257/9296 dev activations (99.6%); the rest are scattered q/y/g/2 cases (18/15/3/3). Nothing fires at L<=5. L-mass shares are 0.012/0.205/0.348/0.435 for L=6..9. Test results reproduce: P=1.0, R=0.894, F1=0.944, mass recall 0.987, with 0 false positives. The L>=6 variant scores F1 0.910 on test, which confirms the stated tradeoff.
